meeting_header: Date: 2026-12-01 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Daniel Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Lumina CTO), Ethan Moore (Lumina ML Eng), Carlos Ruiz (Lumina Security), Hannah Li (Lumina Product)
summary: Discovery call focused on model selection and deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) for Lumina Analytics' multilingual, long-context document understanding product. Main concerns: support for >64k contexts, multilingual performance, tool/function calling, latency vs cost tradeoffs, and enterprise security needs (SOC2, KMS, SSO). Redwood to run benchmarks on candidate open models and send pricing & security docs.
topics: open model comparisons (Llama2, Mistral, Gemma-like, community mixes)
hosting modes: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC/on-prem
security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Daniel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Daniel from Redwood, I'm joined by Maya our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Priya: Hi, thanks, Priya here. doing well. we actually have a tight agenda  model selection and where we land on hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:12] Daniel: Great, that's exactly what we wanted to cover. quick intros? Maya?
[00:16] Maya: Hi all, Maya Singh, SE. I'll be helping with benchmarks and the technical fit.
[00:20] Ethan: Ethan Moore, ML eng  I'm the one running the model evals.
[00:23] Carlos: Carlos Ruiz, security lead.
[00:25] Hannah: Hannah Li, product.
[00:27] Daniel: Cool. Priya, could you share a little bit about your current stack and what success looks like for you on this project?
[00:35] Priya: Sure. We build a document understanding product for enterprise clients  invoices, contracts, multilingual support across EN, ES, FR, PT, and some APAC languages. currently we use a mix of hosted APIs for quick tasks and some self-hosted models for heavy lifting, but we want a single consistent runtime. our big pain points: context length  we need reliable support for 64k-128k tokens for full-document analysis, latency SLAs for interactive flows, and cost predictability. also security: SOC2 and strict KMS requirements.
[01:06] Daniel: Got it. so model-wise are you evaluating closed APIs too or leaning open models?
[01:12] Priya: We're leaning open models for licensing and cost control, but we still need feature parity  tool-calling, function calls, structured outputs. also need strong multilingual quality.
[01:22] Maya: that's helpful. just to align terminology: when you say function calling are you referring to the ability to call external tools/APIs from the model flow (like tool-call, function-call hooks) or more like structured JSON outputs we can parse?
[01:32] Priya: both. we need predictable function calling for retrieval and enrichment, and structured outputs for downstream processing.
[01:38] Ethan: also worth adding we often use a retrieval-augmented pipeline  dense vector DB, then the model with the retrieval context appended; so the KV cache and prefix caching matter for latency.
[01:47] Maya: perfect. on the deployment side, some quick clarifications: Hosted gives fastest time-to-value and Redwood maintains the runtime, Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation, and Private (VPC or on-prem) is for air-gapped/regulatory requirements. which of those map to your needs?
[02:03] Priya: We want to start hosted to move fast, but we expect to need Dedicated within a quarter for predictable SLAs and eventually Private for our larger regulated customers.
[02:12] Daniel: That's a common path. ok let's talk model selection. what are your latency targets and token budgets?
[02:18] Ethan: For the interactive UI we want p95 under 1.2s for 2k-context calls; for batch long-doc summarization latency can be higher, but costs need to stay reasonable. token budgets are variable, some big jobs go to 100k tokens end to end.
[02:33] Maya: so two axes: per-request latency for short/medium contexts and throughput/cost for very long contexts. AWS/TPU-ish hardware aside, some open models support longer context natively (e.g., extended context variants). we can also do chunking with a retrieval approach, but you lose some global coherence.
[02:48] Priya: we tried chunking but it's painful for contracts where cross-references matter. we care about native long context. can Redwood serve 128k contexts?
[02:58] Maya: yes, Redwood's runtime supports long-context execution paths and we have model variants we've verified up to 128k in dedicated/private setups. hosted has practical limits depending on model choice and memory; for the highest contexts we usually recommend Dedicated or Private due to GPU memory and kernel availability.
[03:13] Carlos: on the security side, what's the data residency and KMS story if we go Dedicated? we need customer-managed keys and audit logs.
[03:21] Daniel: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS via integrations and we can push logs to your SIEM, with RBAC and audit trails. Private gives you full control over networking. we'll share the SOC2 and architecture docs.
[03:31] Carlos: ok good. do you have an SOC2 cert?
[03:34] Daniel: yes  we'll share the report. transcription: sometimes the names get messy, we will include the document later.
[03:38] Ethan: back to models  which open models should we consider? we've been testing Llama 2 70B, Mistral 70B, Gemma 70B-ish community replicas. main concerns: multilingual capability and function-calling behavior.
[03:51] Maya: the usual candidates are Llama 2 variants, Mistral large, and various community models (Gemma-ish, OpenAssistant forks). each has tradeoffs: Llama2 is strong with instruction tuning and ecosystem, Mistral has great throughput but some gaps in non-English; recent community models have better multilingual pretraining but less maturity for tool-calling. quantization and kernel support (e.g., optimal CUDA kernels or Triton) will affect latency.
[04:15] Priya: do you support function-calling on open models or is that a Redwood wrapper?
[04:19] Maya: function-calling is implemented in the Redwood runtime as a pluggable layer  we map structured output patterns to function-call events and provide a stable API to your toolchain. the quality depends on the model's instruction compliance, but we can augment with prompt engineering and light fine-tuning.
[04:33] Ethan: about quantization  we want to squeeze costs. what quantization levels are recommended for 70B while preserving multilingual accuracy?
[04:40] Maya: typically we test 4-bit and 5-bit quantization options; some models survive 4-bit better than others. our Optimize toolkit recommends quantization profiles per workload  we run evals on your language set and scoring metrics to recommend a profile. for sensitive production, we often run 5-bit for a middle ground.
[04:57] Priya: can you run benchmarks on our languages? we need Spanish and Portuguese particularly to be robust.
[05:02] Maya: yes, we can run targeted multilingual evals; that's part of the SE scope. we'll do a 5k token long-context test and a 2k interactive suite across EN/ES/PT/FR and a sample APAC language.
[05:14] Daniel: Request: can you share your expected QPS and concurrency? that shapes Dedicated sizing.
[05:19] Priya: For now estimate 50 concurrent interactive users at peak with 100 qps for short calls, and a handful of batch jobs that hit 200 qps for processing windows. 
[05:29] Daniel: makes sense. Dedicated sizing would be ~X GPUs depending on model; we'll include estimates in pricing.
[05:36] Hannah: one question  function calling errors and observability: how do we debug if the model returns malformed JSON or wrong fields?
[05:44] Maya: Redwood Console includes per-request traces, structured output validation hooks, and we can add checkpoints for returned schema validation. if a model drifts we can do rollback to a previous variant and trigger alerts.
[05:55] Carlos: encryption at rest and in-flight? and can we bring our own KMS?
[05:59] Daniel: yes, TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest, and Dedicated/Private support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). we'll attach the compliance doc.
[06:08] Ethan: about fallbacks  if one model fails or is degraded, can you route to a cheaper fallback?
[06:13] Maya: yes, smart routing can fallback to a smaller quantized variant or a cheaper model if latency or capacity constraints are hit. route policies can be per-tenant or per-route.
[06:21] Priya: on billing  how transparent is per-token cost when you do batching and caching?
[06:27] Daniel: Console shows token-level cost and latency breakdowns, with per-route estimates. Optimize suggests batching and cache settings to hit target unit costs.
[06:35] Ethan: technical deep dive  Maya, can you outline the benchmark you'll run for the 5k token test?
[06:40] Maya: sure. we'll pick 3 candidate models (Llama2-70B-extended, Mistral-X-70B, Gemma-community-70B), run native long-context tokenization to 5k, 16k, and 64k windows where supported. measure p50/p95 latency and generation quality on a multilingual prompt set, plus function-calling JSON correctness tests. we'll run quantization profiles (4-bit/5-bit) and include perplexity/ROUGE-like scoring for summarization tasks.
[07:10] Ethan: sounds good. what's the expected turnaround?
[07:12] Maya: we'll start Monday and aim for initial results in 5 business days.
[07:15] Daniel: perfect. Priya, anything else on compliance or procurement timelines?
[07:19] Priya: procurement prefers a 60-day trial window and then a committed Dedicated contract if benchmarks look good. we'll need legal to review the data processing addendum.
[07:29] Daniel: ok we'll include the DPA and SLA examples.
[07:33] Carlos: also need SSO  SAML/Okta  and role-based access.
[07:38] Daniel: supported, we have SAML, OIDC, and granular RBAC.
[07:42] Hannah: question about private deployments: our largest clients require air-gapped on-prem. is Redwood's Private full on-prem or just VPC connectors?
[07:50] Maya: both. Private can be a customer-managed control plane in your VPC or a full on-prem package for regulated customers. integrations for KMS/HSM are supported. there's more setup with on-prem but it's doable.
[07:59] Priya: rough sizing cost  what's order of magnitude for Dedicated for 70B models?
[08:04] Daniel: depends on region and GPU type; ballpark for reserved capacity we'll include in the pricing spreadsheet  the key is commit level and whether you need burst capacity. we'll show examples for 8xA100 vs newer dense-memory GPUs that help with 128k contexts.
[08:19] Ethan: a couple of nitty-gritty items  tokenization differences across models affecting context accounting, and KV cache invalidation when we do retrieval.
[08:26] Maya: yes tokenization matters, and Redwood counts tokens as the model would. KV cache is per-session and can be invalidated programmatically; we provide hooks.
[08:35] Priya: great. also want to confirm data retention: if we use Hosted can you opt-out of storing prompts?
[08:41] Daniel: yes hosted can be configured to not persist request payloads, and for enterprise we offer retention controls plus Private/Dedicated which avoid platform-level retention.
[08:50] Carlos: any third-party pen-tests or reports?
[08:53] Daniel: we have recent pen-test summaries and can share the redacted results.
[08:58] Ethan: ok let's talk about function-calling examples  we need some structured outputs for entity extraction that trigger enrichment calls. can Redwood do sequential tool-calls?
[09:05] Maya: yes, you can orchestrate multiple tool calls; Redwood ties the function-call events to your tool adapters. we also support a retry policy and idempotency tokens.
[09:16] Priya: one more: latency targets for 2k context  you said p95 1.2s  is that realistic with a 70B model?
[09:22] Maya: on Dedicated with optimized kernels and batching we can get near that for 2k windows on modern GPUs; on Hosted it's model dependent but possible with the right variant. we'll confirm in the benchmark.
[09:33] Daniel: time check  we have ~40 minutes left; opening the floor for any other deep technical questions.
[09:38] Ethan: can Redwood's runtime do model composition  e.g., small model for retrieval re-ranking and big model for final synthesis?
[09:43] Maya: yes, route-level composition is supported; can chain models and have staged routing. it's a common pattern.
[09:49] Priya: for multilingual quality, do you recommend fine-tuning on our corpora or retrieval augmentation is enough?
[09:55] Maya: depends  retrieval helps a lot, but for subtle language nuances and domain-specific terms, light fine-tuning or instruction-tuning on your dataset will help. Redwood supports variant management for tuned models.
[10:06] Hannah: procurement will want a sample contract.
[10:09] Daniel: we'll attach a sample SLA and contract template.
[10:13] Priya: ok good. can you also show us the Console during a demo? we'd like to see tracing and cost breakdowns.
[10:20] Daniel: yes we'll schedule a demo session next week to show Console and run through traces.
[10:25] Maya: I'll take the benchmark ownership. we'll need sample doc sets in EN/ES/PT and a small APAC sample. Ethan, can you share those?
[10:33] Ethan: yes I can drop them into the secure share by tomorrow.
[10:36] Carlos: last question on backups  if we go Dedicated who handles patching?
[10:40] Maya: Redwood manages runtime updates for Dedicated and Hosted; for Private on-prem the customer manages the underlying infra but Redwood provides the updater package.
[10:48] Daniel: ok nearing the end, recap of next steps: Daniel send pricing + DPA + SOC2; Maya run benchmarks and deliver results by 2026-12-08; customer to send sample docs and QPS numbers.
[10:58] Priya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[11:01] Daniel: thanks all  we'll follow up with the links.
[52:00] [call ends]
